definition: Any carbon compound except the very simplest ones — carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, the carbonates and the hydrogencarbonates. Originally named for a supposed link to living things, now a structural definition.
msAccepts: not restricted to compounds from living things
msAvoids: saying organic means natural or living-made
omitting the excluded simplest carbon compounds
excluding all compounds with other elements

definition: A compound made up of hydrogen and carbon only. The word only is the definition's load-bearing part: any third element, such as the oxygen in alcohols, disqualifies the compound.
msAccepts: carbon and hydrogen are the only elements
msAvoids: saying contains hydrogen and carbon without 'only'

definition: Describes an organic compound containing only single carbon-carbon bonds. Alkanes are the saturated hydrocarbon family; no further atoms can be added without first breaking a bond.
msAvoids: confusing saturated with unreactive in general
saying it contains maximum hydrogen without the bond logic

definition: Describes an organic compound containing at least one double or triple carbon-carbon bond. The spare bonding capacity of the multiple bond is where addition reactions occur.
msAccepts: contains double or triple C-C bonds
at least one multiple carbon-carbon bond
not all carbon-carbon bonds are single
msAvoids: saying it must contain a triple bond

definition: The simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound. Calculable from experimental data; on its own it cannot identify the true molecular formula.
msAvoids: calling it the actual atom count
claiming it identifies the molecule alone

definition: The actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule of a compound — always a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula. It carries no information about how the atoms are joined.
msAccepts: actual number of each atom in a molecule
a multiple of the empirical formula
msAvoids: saying it shows how atoms are joined
confusing it with the empirical formula always

definition: A formula written with n standing for the carbon count that describes every member of a homologous series at once: CnH2n+2 for alkanes, CnH2n for alkenes, CnH2n+2O for alcohols.
msAccepts: formula for the whole series using n
msAvoids: confusing it with a single molecule's formula
saying it applies across different families

definition: A series of compounds with similar chemical properties because they share the same functional group, consecutive members differing by one CH2 unit. Alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids and esters are examples.
An atom or group of atoms that determines the chemical properties of a compound. All members of the same homologous series carry the same one — −OH for alcohols, C=C for alkenes.
msAccepts: the reactive part of the molecule
msAvoids: saying it only affects physical properties
listing groups without the defining role

definition: A formula showing how the atoms in a molecule are joined together. Drawn condensed (bond lines omitted, e.g. CH3CH2CH3) or displayed (every bond shown as a line).
msAccepts: shows which atoms join to which
condensed form without all bond lines
msAvoids: confusing it with the molecular formula
saying it never shows bonds at all

definition: A structural formula in which every bond is drawn as an individual line, each line representing a shared pair of electrons. Also called the full structural formula.
msAccepts: each line is a shared electron pair
msAvoids: omitting bonds while calling it displayed
confusing it with the condensed form

definition: The naming rules of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry. Names are codes: chain-length code letters, bond-type endings, branch names and position numbers.
msAccepts: chain code plus endings plus positions

definition: The existence of compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae — different compounds because their atoms are joined in a different order. Rotation never converts one isomer into another.
msAccepts: different arrangements with bonds broken to convert

definition: A reaction in which an atom or group of atoms is replaced by a different atom or group. Example: a hydrogen atom of an alkane replaced by a halogen atom, forming a haloalkane and a hydrogen halide.
msAccepts: an atom or group is replaced
something swaps in and something out

definition: A reaction in which something is added to a molecule without taking anything away, using the spare bonding capacity of a double bond. Alkenes undergo them, e.g. ethene plus bromine giving one product.
msAvoids: claiming alkanes add across single bonds
